record.paper_title: Classification of Finite Groups: Recent Developements and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine, and explicitly list up to isomorphism, the groups of order p^n · q where p and q are distinct primes and n ≤ 7. Existing work counts such groups only for n ≤ 5 without listing them, so the problem is to make those arguments constructive enough to produce explicit lists and then extend the classification from n = 5 to the harder cases n = 6 and n = 7, preferably using symbolic calculations because the classifications of groups of order p^6 and p^7 are increasingly complicated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p and q be distinct primes and let n be a positive integer with n ≤ 7. For each such pair (p, q) and each such n, classify up to isomorphism all finite groups of order p^n · q, producing an explicit list of representatives (for example, by presentations or by structural descriptions of their normal Sylow subgroups and the action giving the extension). 

Concretely:
(a) For n ≤ 5, the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order p^n · q is known as a function of p, q, and n; make the enumeration constructive so that it yields an explicit listing of one representative from each isomorphism class.
(b) Extend this explicit classification to n = 6 and n = 7, where the increased complexity of the classification of groups of order p^6 and p^7 makes the problem substantially harder; the use of symbolic computation is permitted and encouraged.

The goal is, for every distinct prime pair (p, q) and every n ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, an explicit, complete, and irredundant list of the groups of order p^n · q up to isomorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: The enumeration by Eick and Moede counts (but does not list) groups of order p^n·q for n ≤ 5. No published work appears to provide an explicit isomorphism-class listing for general (p,q) for n ≤ 5, nor to extend the classification to n = 6 or n = 7. The problem appears to remain open.
